Toxicokinetics
Oral cadmium absorption is high and can be increased by some trace elements such as zinc, iron or calcium. It is transported by
blood cells and the main transport protein in plasma to the kidneys is the metallothionein, a low molecular weight protein cysteine-
rich with numerous thiol binding sites. Metallothionein is induced by cadmium exposure and can be ﬁltered through the kidney
glomerular membrane (when its binding capacity is exceeded, renal toxicity occurs) (Gil, 2018).
Cadmium is distributed to various organs and tissues, mainly (more than 70%) to liver, muscles and kidneys, the latter being the
target organs. Excretion is through the urine and at a very low rate, which justiﬁes its extensive accumulation in the organism (the
half-life in the kidney cortex and liver can be as long as 20–25 years).
Toxicity
As indicated above, the most important target organ is the kidney, which justiﬁes that most of the manifestations that characterize
